claims.text: Depositing a thin, conformal Al2O3 coating by ALD on a refractory high-entropy alloy will significantly improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
An untreated AlNbTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy forms non-protective oxide scales during high-temperature exposure.
ALD treatment will produce a continuous alumina layer on the alloy surface.
The ALD-produced alumina layer will be dense and adherent.
An alumina surface layer can act as a protective oxidation barrier on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The alumina coating limits oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
The alumina coating suppresses the formation of fast-growing, non-protective oxides.
Al2O3 is thermodynamically stable under high-temperature oxidation conditions.
Alumina has a slow growth rate at high temperatures, which slows alloy oxidation.
After 100 hours at approximately 1000°C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere, the ALD-coated alloy will have significantly lower mass gain than the untreated alloy.
After the specified exposure, the ALD-coated alloy will have a more protective and adherent oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically develop fast-growing, non-protective oxide scales with high mass gain under similar conditions.
Oxidation of refractory high-entropy alloys can cause severe degradation of mechanical properties.
The coating is expected to be effective under static exposure around 1000°C.
Performance under thermal cycling, substantially higher temperatures, or imperfect coating uniformity is uncertain.
Prior evidence supports the protective nature of ALD-deposited alumina in related systems.
The quantitative improvement and long-term adhesion of ALD alumina on specific refractory high-entropy alloys have not been fully determined.
